corporate_treasury_listed.name: Polaris Industrial Holdings PJSC — Corporate Treasury
corporate_treasury_listed.narrative:
Polaris Industrial Holdings PJSC is a UAE-listed corporate holding group
with multi-currency operating accounts and a long-dated corporate-finance
facility. Three signatories exercise the spec's full PartyType /
AccountRole vocabulary: a senior managing official and a power-of-
attorney holder operate the accounts jointly (any-two operating mandate
realised in spec terms as PartyType=Joint), with an administrator on
Delegate authority for day-to-day operations. Customer inflows are
monthly invoiced from B2B counterparties; supplier outflows are
cross-border in USD/EUR. The persona exercises corporate-grade KYC and
identity-assurance fields (PartyCategory=Corporate plus the verified-
claims block on the Party records) that retail and SME personas don't
reach.

gig_variable_income.name: Priya — Gig / Variable Income
gig_variable_income.narrative:
Priya works gig hours via delivery and rideshare platforms. Her income
arrives in irregular bursts from multiple counterparties — no single
Flags=Payroll credit marks her salary. EXP-18's primary income formula
(trailing-12-month average of Payroll-flagged credits) returns nothing
for her; the Phase 1.5 Underwriting panel must fall back to Fallback B
(clustered counterparty inflow) to produce a usable income signal.

hnw_multicurrency.name: Layla — HNW Multi-Currency Holder
hnw_multicurrency.narrative:
Layla holds AED current + USD/EUR/GBP savings accounts. Regular FX
transfers (2–6/month, in USD/EUR/GBP) exercise the v2.1 CurrencyExchange
block: SourceCurrency, TargetCurrency, ExchangeRate, InstructedAmount.
Premium-product LFI configurations populate optional fields aggressively
on her bundle; sparse-LFI mode shows how thin the international-transfer
shape can become when those optionals drop out.

joint_account_family.name: Maria & Rohan — Joint Account / Family
joint_account_family.narrative:
Maria & Rohan are an expat couple with a joint current account and a
custodian-for-minor savings account for their two children. Tests the
v2.1 multi-party shapes: PartyType=Joint, AccountRole=CustodianForMinor.
Bundle exercises /accounts/{AccountId}/parties heavily (multiple Party
records per account).

mortgage_dbr_heavy.name: Yousef — Mortgage Holder (DBR Heavy)
mortgage_dbr_heavy.narrative:
Yousef is salaried at AED 32k with a long-dated mortgage. Total fixed
commitments — mortgage principal, school fees, utilities, car finance —
push his implied DBR comfortably above 60%. The Phase 1.5 Underwriting
panel will compute Total Fixed Commitments by summing standing-order
NextPaymentAmount + direct-debit PreviousPaymentAmount, normalised to
monthly via Frequency. This persona is the DBR stress case.

nsf_distressed.name: Hadi — NSF / Distressed Borrower
nsf_distressed.narrative:
Hadi is salaried at AED 11.5k with rent + utilities + telco + a personal-
loan repayment that together leave little buffer. Late-month direct-debit
rejections are routine — Status="Rejected" on roughly half the months
in the trailing window. EXP-18's NSF / distress event count exercises
this persona heavily; behavioural-distress monitoring rules can use this
shape as a positive case.

recent_graduate_thin_file.name: Tanvi — Recent Graduate (Thin File)
recent_graduate_thin_file.narrative:
Tanvi is a junior IT analyst, salaried at AED 8.5k, single account opened
8 months ago. She splits rent with flatmates via a shared standing order.
Tests thin-file underwriting: short-tenure account, low-value transactions,
little fixed-commitment surface. EXP-18 low-volume guard may engage at the
margin (8 months × ~30 tx/month ≈ 240 — above the 50-tx floor but distinct
months below the 12 expected).

salaried_emirati_affluent.name: Khalid — Salaried Emirati (Affluent)
salaried_emirati_affluent.narrative:
Khalid is a 45-year-old Emirati national in Abu Dhabi, salaried at AED
60k/mo, with a mortgage, a savings account, a high-limit credit card,
and several monthly commitments (school fees, club membership, utilities).
Tests multi-account stress, high-DBR commitments, and a Sharia-compliant
mortgage product. Salary lands on the 27th, mortgage principal hits the
next day.

salaried_expat_mid.name: Sara — Salaried Expat (Mid Tier)
salaried_expat_mid.narrative:
Sara is an IT professional in Dubai, salaried at AED 25k/mo from a tech-sector
free-zone employer. She has a current account she has held for 2 years and one
credit card. Her rent direct debit hits two days after her 25th-of-the-month
salary; utilities and telco are predictable mid-month direct debits. No FX, no
cash deposits — a classic "baseline affordability case" persona that exercises
the spec-clean Flags=Payroll salary marker and the optional CreditLine block.

senior_retiree.name: Hassan — Senior / Retiree
senior_retiree.narrative:
Hassan is 68, retired, receiving a GCC pension on the 1st of each month.
Low transaction volume by design — typically <10 transactions/month.
Triggers EXP-18's low-volume guard under all three LFI profiles: the
trailing-12-month-count is below the 50-transaction floor, so the
Underwriting panel suppresses DBR with a tooltip explaining why. The
Senior persona is the case study for "off-the-shelf affordability
formulas don't generalise to low-volume segments."

sme_cash_heavy.name: Karim — SME Owner (Cash-Heavy Retail)
sme_cash_heavy.narrative:
Karim runs a retail shop in Sharjah. Most receipts are cash deposited
into the current account in bursts (4–14 deposits/month, AED 800–8k each).
Sparse merchant detail because the bank can't categorise teller deposits
the way it can POS transactions. A shop-rent standing order and a POS-
terminal-lease direct debit are the only fixed commitments. AML stress
case: behavioural-monitoring rules need to handle cash-dominant accounts.

sme_clinic_receivables.name: Crestline Wellness Clinic LLC — Healthcare Clinic
sme_clinic_receivables.narrative:
Crestline Wellness Clinic is a single-location DHA-licensed mainland
clinic owned by the practising physician (Sole signatory) with a
practice manager added under Administrator / Delegate for AP and
insurer-portal reconciliation. The cash-flow stress is insurance-
receivable aging: 30–60-day lag from claim submission through e-claim
platform fee deduction to net-of-co-pay reimbursement from a small
set of dominant insurer-payor counterparties. Walk-in card receipts
and small-amount cash deposits land daily; insurer payouts arrive
irregularly in larger chunks. Operating account on a Tier-1
conventional bank; Islamic deposit secondary for the partner-draw
savings; digital-challenger tertiary to test the working-capital
facility some SME-fintechs price aggressively against insurance
receivables. Stress: payor-tagged inflow stream, 30–60-day inflow
lag distinct from other personas, mixed retail-card and B2B-credit
flow on one operating account — bridges banking-domain personas with
the insurance-domain motor personas without crossing into Open
Insurance scope.

sme_construction_pdc.name: Meridian Build Works LLC — Construction Sub-Contractor
sme_construction_pdc.narrative:
Meridian Build Works is a Sharjah-mainland sub-contractor on civil
works — certified-payment-based receivables from a small set of main
contractors, milestone-billed and irregular. Inflows arrive 30–60
days after certification, often net of 5–10% retention; some are
post-dated cheques. Two signatories: the principal owner (Sole) and
a delegated power-of-attorney holder authorised for cheque deposit
and yard-supplier AP. ~80 labourers on a single monthly WPS batch is
the dominant outflow. Retention release lands as occasional large
unbatched lump-sum credits months after the original certification.
Operating account is a Tier-1 conventional bank; secondary at an
Islamic bank for term deposit of the principal's own savings. NSF
events occur 1–4 per year — typical for the working-capital squeeze
of milestone-billed civil-works SMEs. Stress: PDC handling, retention
release matching, large-batch WPS payroll — none of which the existing
SME personas exercise.

sme_ecommerce_marketplace.name: Indigo Storefront FZ-LLC — E-commerce Marketplace Seller
sme_ecommerce_marketplace.narrative:
Indigo Storefront sells consumer-electronics and home goods across
multiple online channels: a marketplace-aggregator presence, a brand-
owned Shopify-style storefront, and direct-to-consumer Instagram
orders. Inflows are bi-weekly net-of-commission marketplace payouts,
card-payment-gateway daily payouts (separately netted of processing
fees), and irregular courier COD remittances. AED operating account
for domestic flows; a USD operating account for international supplier
wires (FX-active). Two structurally distinct PSPs and one marketplace
payor across three settlement cadences make the gross-to-net
reconciliation the core accounting pain — and the strongest argument
for OF-fed bank feeds in lieu of monthly PSP-portal CSVs. SME-digital-
challenger primary banker, conventional Tier-1 secondary, foreign-
branch trade-finance tertiary for the supplier-wire corridor.

sme_fnb_multi_outlet.name: Saffron Plate Group LLC — F&B Multi-Outlet Operator
sme_fnb_multi_outlet.narrative:
Saffron Plate Group operates a 3-outlet café-and-casual-dining chain
across Dubai Marina and JBR. The principal owner is the sole signatory
on the operating account; an outlet-manager delegate is added under
Administrator / Delegate for day-to-day reconciliation. Inflows are
weekly aggregator payouts net of platform commission (booked against
the aggregator-commission DD), plus daily POS settlements that sweep
into the operating account from the acquiring relationship — a
structurally separate LFI from the operating bank. Two outlet rents,
utilities, and a POS-terminal lease are the fixed commitments; payroll
is a single ~86k AED WPS batch monthly. The reconciliation stress is
the gap between gross orders, aggregator commission, refunds, and
daily settlement timing — a TPP-side accounting integration over OF
collapses three EOD CSVs into one journal.

sme_rak_trading_emirati.name: Falcon Pearl General Trading LLC — RAK Free-Zone Trading SME
sme_rak_trading_emirati.narrative:
Falcon Pearl General Trading is a RAKEZ free-zone-licensed trading
company owned by an Emirati principal with his brother as joint
secondary owner; the operations manager (an expat-Arab finance
professional) holds Power-of-Attorney on the operating account. The
principal lives between Ras Al Khaimah and Sharjah; the warehouse and
back-office sit inside the RAK free zone. Inflows are monthly B2B
invoices to UAE-mainland customers; supplier outflows go cross-border
in USD/EUR for finished goods. Tier-2-conventional primary banker
is realistic for Northern-Emirates SMEs that prefer regional
relationships over the Tier-1 Abu Dhabi / Dubai brands; Islamic-deposit
secondary holds the principal's term-deposit and the zakat-distribution
standing order; foreign-branch trade-finance tertiary handles the
international wire corridor. Stress: first persona to anchor at a
Tier-2 conventional primary slot, first Emirati-owned SME, first
Northern-Emirates persona — exercises the demographic + bank-tier
dimensions the Dubai/Sharjah-skewed SME set doesn't reach.

sme_saas_freezone.name: Talisman Software FZ-LLC — Free-Zone SaaS Startup
sme_saas_freezone.narrative:
Talisman Software is a Series-A SaaS company licensed in a Dubai free
zone (DIFC-style flavour) with a small distributed team. Customer
inflows are monthly USD subscription receipts from international
customers, settled into the USD operating account. Supplier outflows
are USD cloud-infrastructure charges (compute, observability, identity
services). AED operating account holds the WPS payroll batch and the
AED-denominated office lease + DEWA. A USD savings account holds
Series-A runway. Two co-founders are joint signatories on the AED
operating account; an operations-manager delegate is added for AP
reconciliation. FX-active edge of the v2.1 spec exercised by the
USD-AED dual-currency operating reality and FX-rate-bearing cross-
account transfers. Trade-finance secondary at a foreign-branch bank
for the international wire corridor; digital-challenger tertiary for
founder card / expense reimbursement.

sme_trading_business.name: Aurora Trading LLC — SME Trading Business
sme_trading_business.narrative:
Aurora Trading LLC is a Dubai-mainland SME that imports finished goods
from international suppliers and resells to UAE wholesale customers.
Two signatories on the business accounts: the principal owner (Sole)
and a delegated power-of-attorney holder authorised to operate the
account on the principal's behalf. Customer inflows arrive on a
biweekly cadence from local B2B counterparties; supplier outflows go
cross-border in USD/EUR, exercising the FX-active edge of the v2.1
Bank Data Sharing transaction set. AccountType=SME, PartyCategory=SME,
PartyType=Delegate exercise the v2.1-errata1 business-account spec
surface that retail personas don't reach.

counterparty_banks_uae_real.description:
Real UAE counterparty banks (D-14). Banks named in this pool appear as
third-party counterparties to the persona's transactions, standing
orders, scheduled payments, and beneficiaries — i.e., the bank on the
OTHER side of an outbound transfer or inbound credit. Naming a real
bank here is descriptive of the persona's relationships, not an
operational claim about the named bank's data quality. NG5 / D-14
forbid the same names from appearing in any populate-rate context or
as the bundle-emitting LFI.

Per-bank fields:
  - `iban_prefix` (4-char "AE" + 2-digit) — kept for back-compat with
    generator paths that don't yet have a full bank object. New code
    paths use `bank_code` instead.
  - `bank_code` (3-digit synthetic CBUAE-style bank code) — embedded at
    IBAN positions 5–7 by `drawIban()`. Each bank has a unique code
    (derived from `iban_prefix`'s 2 digits + '0'); mod-97 check digits
    are computed over the BBAN so every issued IBAN passes ISO-13616
    validation. Synthetic — NOT the bank's real CBUAE-assigned routing
    code (encoding real codes would imply operational attribution per
    NG5).
  - `bic` (8-char synthetic BIC stem) — used as
    CreditorAgent.Identification (SchemeName=BICFI). Format follows the
    ISO-9362 BIC8 shape `BBBBAEXX` where BBBB is a synthetic mnemonic
    derived from the bank name + AE country + XX synthetic location.
    It is structurally a valid BIC8 but is NOT the bank's real CBUAE-
    assigned routing identifier (real BICs are not encoded — that
    would imply operational attribution per NG5).

Coverage: post-2024 CBUAE-licensed bank set, organised by tier and
type so the generator's RNG draws yield a UAE-realistic mix across
any persona's transaction stream.

banks.name: National Bank of Umm Al Quwain

ibans_synthetic.description:
IBANs in this sandbox use the AE prefix and a synthetic 21-digit body so they
are structurally valid (length 23) but do not collide with real-world UAE
IBANs assigned by the central bank. The body is generated deterministically
from (persona_id, account_index, seed) — see src/generator/identity.js.
